newsitem.title: HONG KONG: People leap from building to escape Hong Kong blaze.
newsitem.headline: People leap from building to escape Hong Kong blaze.

text.p: People leapt from windows or clung by their fingertips to air conditioners on the wall of a Hong Kong commercial high-rise building as fire swept through lower floors on Wednesday.

A dramatic rescue was launched by Hong Kong firefighters to save scores of people believed trapped in the 16-floor building on the bustling Nathan Road, heart of the Kowloon tourist shopping district.
The fire broke out on the ground floor.
Terrified people jumped from window ledges on to rescue ladders and others scrambled on to ledges and air conditioners.
About 50 people had been rescued after three hours of the rescue effort as the fire sent high flames and a darkening cloud over the Kowloon peninsula. The cause of the fire was not clear.
All those rescued were ferried to hospital, the Hong Kong government said. No deaths were reported and the seriousness of the injuries was not immediately revealed.
An unknown number of people were still trapped inside the building which was engulfed in smoke.
